accepted.s: Who succeeded Nizam Nasir-ud-Daula in Hyderabad in 1857?
accepted.x: Afzal-ud-Daula succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula in 1857 and ruled Hyderabad from 1857 to 1869.
accepted.tq: Use the direct succession clue and distinguish the Nizam from the other Hyderabad figures.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hyderabad in 1857:
1. Nasir-ud-Daula died on 16 May 1857.
2. Afzal-ud-Daula retained Salar Jung I as his Diwan.
3. Both the Nizam and Salar Jung supported the British during the revolt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Nasir-ud-Daula died on 16 May 1857; Afzal-ud-Daula retained Mir Turab Ali Khan, known as Salar Jung I, and both remained pro-British.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently, especially the succession date and the political alignment of the Nizam and Diwan.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mir Turab Ali Khan, who continued as Diwan under Afzal-ud-Daula, was better known as
accepted.x: Mir Turab Ali Khan was Salar Jung I, the Diwan retained by Afzal-ud-Daula.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between formal names and titles of the principal Hyderabad officials.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The outbreak at Aurangabad in June 1857 was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Mir Fida Ali and Amir Khan
accepted.x: The Aurangabad outbreak was associated with Mir Fida Ali and Amir Khan. It was suppressed by Captain Abbot, and Fida Ali was hanged.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure person-event pair and reject leaders belonging to other risings.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Aurangabad outbreak of June 1857, consider the following statements:
1. The 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent came under suspicion.
2. The suspected cavalry unit was disarmed.
3. Mir Fida Ali was transported for life to the Andamans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 1st Cavalry came under suspicion and was disarmed; Mir Fida Ali was hanged, whereas Maulvi Allauddin was transported to the Andamans.
accepted.tq: Separate the punishments of Fida Ali and Allauddin before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The immediate objective of Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin in attacking the British Residency at Hyderabad was to
accepted.x: The attack was undertaken to free Jamedar Chida Khan, who had been arrested and held at Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate purpose of an action rather than the broader background grievance.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who repulsed the attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad on 17 July 1857?
accepted.x: Resident Davidson repulsed the attack led by Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin.
accepted.tq: Use the action-person association and distinguish the Residency defender from the Aurangabad suppressor.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Captain Abbot — led the attack on the British Residency
Maulvi Allauddin — transported for life to the Andamans
Mir Fida Ali — escaped and was later shot near Toopran
Turrebaz Khan — hanged immediately after the Aurangabad outbreak
accepted.x: Maulvi Allauddin was transported for life to the Andamans. Turrebaz Khan escaped, was later captured and shot near Toopran in 1859; Captain Abbot suppressed the Aurangabad outbreak.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched person and punishment while rejecting swapped roles and outcomes.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Turrebaz Khan, after escaping from Hyderabad, was eventually captured and shot near
accepted.x: Turrebaz Khan was captured and shot near Toopran in 1859.
accepted.tq: Test the precise place associated with the later fate of a rebellion leader.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following rewards was conferred after Hyderabad remained loyal to the British in 1857?
o: Afzal-ud-Daula received the Star of India.
Mir Fida Ali was appointed Diwan.
Maulvi Allauddin was restored to Hyderabad.
Turrebaz Khan received the Star of India.
accepted.x: Afzal-ud-Daula received the Star of India. Salar Jung I was honoured, and Raichur Doab and Dharaseo were restored while a debt was written off.
accepted.tq: Match the reward with the loyal ruler, not with a rebel or military officer.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following territories was restored to Hyderabad as part of the rewards for its loyalty?
accepted.x: Raichur Doab and Dharaseo, identified with Osmanabad, were restored to Hyderabad; a debt was also written off.
accepted.tq: Separate the territories restored as a reward from regions associated with grievances or rebellions.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in Hyderabad in chronological order:
A. Arrest of Mubariz-ud-Daula
B. Aurangabad outbreak and disarming of the 1st Cavalry
C. Arrest and detention of Jamedar Chida Khan
D. Attack on the British Residency by Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin
accepted.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, the Aurangabad episode occurred in June 1857, Chida Khan was then detained, and the Residency was attacked on 17 July 1857.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then distinguish the June episode from the July attack.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with the Wahabi conspiracy, was imprisoned in
accepted.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula, a Wahabi leader, was imprisoned in Golconda Fort in 1839.
accepted.tq: Link the leader with the specific place of imprisonment rather than with the later Residency episode.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad in 1857 - Residency attack, Turrebaz Khan, Maulvi Allauddin, Nizam and Salar Jung  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gulugonda/Ganjam agency rising — Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi
accepted.x: The Rampa rebellion occurred in 1879, whereas Mubariz-ud-Daula was associated with the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy. Taranikallu, Gulugonda/Ganjam and Uyyalawada are correctly matched with the persons shown.
accepted.tq: Look for the swapped leader-event association among otherwise familiar regional rebellions.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mutakuri Goudappa, who was hanged, was associated with the 1801 disturbance at
accepted.x: The 1801 Taranikallu disturbance in Adoni was associated with Patel Mutakuri Goudappa, who was hanged.
accepted.tq: Combine the year, place and individual to identify the correct regional event.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gulugonda/Ganjam Agency rising of 1845–48 was associated with
accepted.x: Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi were associated with the Gulugonda/Ganjam Agency rising of 1845–48.
accepted.tq: Match the regional rising with its local leaders while eliminating names from other Hyderabad risings.

accepted.s: Which of the following events occurred in 1853?
o: The Residency at Hyderabad was attacked.
accepted.x: Opposition to the Berar assignment occurred in 1853. The Residency attack was in 1857, the Rampa rebellion in 1879, and Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in 1839.
accepted.tq: Use the year-event pair and reject events belonging to nearby but different dates.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an event of 1857 in the Hyderabad State or Andhra region?
accepted.x: The Dandasena disturbance occurred on 9 August 1857. The Residency attack was on 17 July, and the Peer Saheb episode at Kadapa was on 28 August.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced dates of the 1857 regional disturbances.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the other 1857-era risings in Hyderabad State?
o: Ganjam under Korra Mallayya and Chinna Bhupathi
accepted.x: Ganjam was associated with the 1845–48 Agency rising, not the list of other 1857-era Hyderabad State risings. Sholapur, Chanda and Nanded are correctly associated with the persons stated.
accepted.tq: Find the event from a different period within a list of otherwise contemporary risings.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a 1857-era rising in Hyderabad State?
accepted.x: Ramji Gond was associated with the Adilabad rising. Rangarao Pagi belonged to Nanded, Rohilla to Nirmal, and Bapurao with Venkatarao to Chanda.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate leaders assigned to neighbouring risings.
accepted.sec: Chronology of rebellions in Hyderabad State and Andhra  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a reason for the limited response to the Revolt of 1857 in Andhra?
o: The zamindars lost all benefits under the Permanent Settlement.
The people rejected the stability of Company rule.
The Madras Presidency became the principal centre of the revolt.
The Nizam and Salar Jung remained loyal to the British.
accepted.x: The Nizam and Salar Jung remained pro-British, while the Madras Presidency was generally quiet. Zamindars benefited from the Permanent Settlement and many people valued the stability of Company rule.
accepted.tq: Identify the political and social condition that reduced the spread of rebellion.
accepted.sec: Reasons for limited response in Andhra (assertion-reason)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the limited response in Andhra:
1. Public meetings expressing loyalty were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada.
2. Many people preferred the stability of Company rule to the earlier anarchy.
3. Andhra had no local leaders capable of organising resistance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because local leaders and disturbances, including Turrebaz Khan, Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena, did exist.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim that the region had no local leaders while retaining the documented loyalty factors.
accepted.sec: Reasons for limited response in Andhra (assertion-reason)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The response to the Revolt of 1857 in Andhra was limited and scattered.
Reason (R): Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I remained pro-British.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the pro-British position of the Nizam and his Diwan was an important reason why the revolt did not spread widely in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Test whether the political alignment stated in the Reason directly accounts for the limited regional response.
accepted.sec: Reasons for limited response in Andhra (assertion-reason)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following places was NOT mentioned as a venue of loyalty meetings in Andhra during the Revolt of 1857?
accepted.x: Loyalty meetings were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada. Kadiri was associated with an attempt to incite rebellion in Rayalaseema, not with the listed loyalty meetings.
accepted.tq: Distinguish places linked with loyalty from a place associated with an attempted rebellion.
accepted.sec: Reasons for limited response in Andhra (assertion-reason)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains the principal background grievances connected with discontent in Hyderabad State and Andhra before or during 1857?
o: The 1794 battle, the 1846–47 rising and the 1879 Rampa rebellion only
The Permanent Settlement, the Star of India and the restoration of Dharaseo
The 1800 cession, the 1839 Wahabi conspiracy and the 1853 Berar treaty
The 1857 Residency attack, the 1862 conspiracy and the 1801 hanging only
accepted.x: The major background grievances identified were the 1800 cession, the Wahabi conspiracy of 1839 and the 1853 Berar treaty, involving Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad/Dharashiv.
accepted.tq: Group the underlying grievances together rather than confusing them with later events or rewards.
accepted.sec: Reasons for limited response in Andhra (assertion-reason)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Peshwa Rao, also referred to as Ramarao, was associated with the conspiracy of
accepted.x: Peshwa Rao, or Ramarao, was associated with the 1862 conspiracy and was caught at Kanpur.
accepted.tq: Match the person with the distinct year of the conspiracy, avoiding the more prominent 1857 events.
